Hi Evan — thanks for the note and the clear questions. Looping in Marissa (compliance) and Mina (security) so they can add the precise acceptance criteria. Quick answers and follow-ups below: 

- Report age: our standard is to accept a pen test report performed within 12 months of the procurement review date for SOC 2 purposes. In specific cases (e.g., long procurement timelines) we can consider up to 18 months if accompanied by evidence of continuous remediation and a recent internal retest.

- Redacted reports: yes — we accept redacted reports for procurement and initial security review, provided the redaction does not remove: scope definition, test dates, findings severity classification, and remediation status. We require artifacts to support the redactions (see list below).

- Vendor creds: we prefer vendors with an established track record (3+ years) and an industry-recognized profile (CREST accreditation, OSCP-certified testers on the engagement, or equivalent). For smaller boutique firms we ask for sample engagement letters and references.

Acceptable supporting artifacts (we commonly request these):
- Signed engagement letter that names Redwood and scope (PDF)
- Redacted full report OR executive summary (PDF)
- Evidence of remediation/verification (screenshots, test logs, retest summary)
- Vendor creds (one-pager or accreditation PDF)

I’m attaching a short summary we send to customers that explains our acceptance criteria. Marissa / Mina — please add anything I missed and confirm the 12-month baseline.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Evan — thanks for reaching out. Adding a bit more formality to Karthik’s note (we use this language in our vendor acceptance doc):

1) Age 
- Baseline: 12 months maximum at the time of security review.
- Exceptions: up to 18 months if accompanied by a documented remediation plan and evidence of verification (e.g., retest or scan showing closed/mitigated findings).

2) Redaction policy 
- Redacted reports are acceptable for procurement and NDAs. Required unredacted items (even if redacted for external consumption) must be available under a mutual NDA or via a gated upload: scope, finding titles and severities, and remediation status.

3) Vendor qualifications 
- Preferred: CREST-accredited firms or equivalent.
- Minimum: testers with verifiable certifications (OSCP, CISSP for lead reviewer) and 2+ enterprise engagements.
- We also accept a vendor one-pager plus two enterprise references.

4) Evidence we typically require with a redacted report 
- Signed engagement letter (scope and dates)
- Redacted report or executive summary (PDF)
- Screenshots of verification / retest results or a short retest addendum
- Vendor creds (PDF) and contact for reference checks

Attachment: I’m attaching our formal acceptance checklist for procurement to include with the SOW. If your procurement team needs any language changes we can provide a short addendum.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference

Evan / team — quick technical clarifications from the security ops side: 

- Methodology: we expect tests to align with common industry standards (OWASP Top 10 for web apps, NIST SP 800-115 for network/host testing, and authenticated test coverage where applicable). Automated scans alone are not sufficient.

- Scope expectations: production-like environment, representative datasets (PII endpoints can be excluded if explicitly out-of-scope but we will ask for compensating controls evidence).

- Retest/verification: When findings are marked as remediated we want either a vendor retest report (preferred) or internal verification artifacts (screenshots, test logs, PRs referencing fixes). For high/critical findings we require vendor verification within 30 days of remediation.

- Report age nuance: the 12-month clock starts on the last test date in the report (not report publication date). If you have rolling tests across modules, please submit the most recent test date per component.

If it helps, I can run a short 30-minute intake call to review the actual artifacts and confirm acceptance for your procurement team. I’ve opened an internal follow-up ticket: SUP-1423 to track an evidence upload and possible retest scheduling.

Thanks,
